name: Week 15 Legs — Steady State, Station-Grouped (Spotlight: Leg Press + Bulgarian)
description: Volume steady, station-grouped. Squat holds 75 with the 6/7/8/8 ascending pyramid that produced good depth (depth built UP across the ramp last week, so it stays). Spotlights cycle forward to leg press (drill the full-ROM knees-to-chest depth — it's been training the abs/QL more than the legs three weeks running) and Bulgarian split squat (step the load up — the single-40 last week had headroom). Leg curl stays before incline RDL so the two hamstring lifts don't stack.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state, station-grouped. Squat holds 75 / 6/7/8/8 (depth builds across the ramp). Leg press + Bulgarian get the spotlight — leg press for the full-ROM core/QL depth, Bulgarian for the load step-up. Leg curl before incline RDL so the hamstring work doesn't stack.

spotlights.why: The full-ROM knees-to-chest position has trained the abs/QL/core more than the legs three weeks running — the user feels it there, not in the quads. Spotlight drills the depth + the active brace that keeps the lower back from lifting off the pad. Depth is the work; the load holds at 3 plates.

Stepped from bodyweight (W13) to a single 40lb DB (W14) clean, no twitching, 'could go heavier.' The step-up is earned — spotlight drills the front-heel drive + vertical-torso pattern at the new load so the form leads the weight.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W12 seated leg curl + calf raise · W13 Bulgarian split squat (NEW) · W14 squat + incline RDL · W15 leg press + Bulgarian (current) · W16 cycle forward — squat depth or calf-raise single-leg.
watchpoints: **Loads hold** — squat 75/side, leg press 3 plates, calf raise 3 plates, leg curl 90, incline RDL 45lb plate. The Bulgarian steps up (see its notes).
**Squat holds 6/7/8/8 at 75.** Depth built UP across the ascending ramp last week (the later sets were the deepest) — keep working the depth here, don't add load.
**Station-grouped sequence:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (SAME machine, stay there) → Bulgarian (bench station) → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Keep leg curl BEFORE incline RDL.** Running them reversed (incline RDL first) stacked two hamstring lifts back-to-back and smoked the second — keep the prescribed order.
**Bulgarian step-up** — single 45-50lb DB or a 25lb pair (your call on the carry). If anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight and finish — that's the standing rule on this lift.
**QL/psoas watch** — cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down. If anything talks in the warmup, modify the day; mid-session, drop a set.

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release)

exercises.notes: Full depth, slow. Find where the hips are tight and breathe into it. Depth check before loading.

30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — the stretch runs down the side of the waist into the QL and lateral hip. Do this before loading the squat.
Big slow circles. Wake up the hip stabilizers.
Spine mobility — slow, full ROM each direction.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension. Quick posterior-chain and low-back opener before loading the squat.
Bodyweight. QL check — if anything talks here, modify the day. Also previews the Bulgarian pattern.
Set 1: 45/side x8. Set 2: 65/side x8. Same depth as the working sets.

**LOAD:** 75/side. 4 sets: **6 / 7 / 8 / 8**. The depth built up across the ramp last week — keep working it at 75, that's the win.
- Bar high on the upper traps (NOT the neck), upper-back shelf squeezed
- **Brace like prepping for a punch** — deep belly breath at the top, HOLD through the descent, exhale on the drive up
- **Hips back AND down**, not just down
- 'Spread the floor' — screw the feet into the ground
- Knees track over the toes
- **Sit into the bottom** — the later sets were the deepest last week; keep chasing that depth, set by set
- Drive through the WHOLE foot

**Reflection:** the deepest reps last week came on the 7- and 8-rep sets, not the opening 6. Does that hold again — does depth keep building across the ramp? If it does, 6/7/8/8 at 75 is the durable pattern.

sets.name: 🔆 Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine — Spotlight: Leg Press Depth)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 3 plates/side. 4 sets of 12. Chase DEPTH, not load.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the full-ROM core/QL position:**
- **Foot position:** shoulder-width, mid-foot on the platform, slight toe-out — set this before loading
- **Full ROM — knees toward the chest** ('knees hitting chest'). This deep position is what's been training the abs/QL/core more than the quads — that's the intent, not a bug
- **Actively press to keep the lower back from lifting off the pad** at the bottom — the brace is the spotlight; if the hips roll off the pad, you've gone past your current control, back off a hair
- **Press through the WHOLE foot** — heels grounded
- **Slow descent (3s), no bounce at the bottom**
- **Don't lock out hard at the top** — leave a hair of bend. Breath: in on the descent, out on the drive

**Reflection:** where does the work land — abs/QL/core (the pattern of the last three weeks) or the legs? If it's still core-dominant at full depth, that's the lift doing its job; hold 3 plates and keep the depth.

sets.name: Leg-Press Calf Raise (Same Machine — Stays Right Here)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 3 plates/side. 3 sets of 15. Stay on the leg press — same machine, no walking off.
- **Balls of both feet on the BOTTOM EDGE of the platform, heels hanging off** — no plate under the foot, the platform edge gives the heel drop
- **Both feet on the platform** — double-leg
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the heels drop as far below the edge as they'll go
- **Drive to FULL plantarflexion at the top**
- **3-4s eccentric** — the slow descent is the stimulus, not added load
- **1s squeeze at the peak**, no bouncing. Breath continuous, don't hold.

The slow tempo bit hard at this load last week — hold 3 plates; the single-leg conversation waits until the eccentric is dialed at double-leg.

sets.name: 🔆 Bulgarian Split Squat (Bench Station — Spotlight: Load Step-Up)

exercises.equipment: bench + DBs — Smith machine if free (use smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** step up — **single 45-50lb DB (goblet/suitcase) or a 25lb pair at the sides**, your call on the carry. The single-40 last week was 'decently hard... could go heavier.' 3 sets of 8-10 each leg.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — let the form lead the load:**
- **Rear foot up on the bench** behind you, laces down or toes tucked
- **Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly VERTICAL at the bottom** — too short a stance = the knee crashes past the toes
- **Front knee tracks over the front foot** — not caving in
- **Lower until the rear knee nearly touches the floor** — controlled, no dropping
- **Drive up through the FRONT HEEL** — the front leg does the work, the rear leg is a kickstand for balance
- **Torso TALL** — a slight forward lean is fine, no folding over
- **2s descent**, own the bottom

**Watch:** if anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight for the remaining sets and finish — going too heavy too fast is what triggered spasms on prior unprogrammed attempts. The step-up is deliberate, not a jump.

**Reflection:** does the front-heel drive + vertical torso hold at the heavier load, or does the form start leaning/cheating? If it holds clean, this is the new working load; if it cheats, the single-40 was the right number.

sets.name: Seated Leg Curl (3 Sets at 90 — Before Incline RDL)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 90. 3 sets of 12, slow tempo — you feel these deeply when you go slow.
- **Ankles UNDER the pad** — the ankle bone is the contact point, NOT the mid-calf
- **Settings: 5/m/0/1** (verify before loading)
- **Lap pad locked DOWN firmly** — a loose pad lets the torso lift and turns it into lower-back work
- **Curl the heels toward the glutes** — full ROM, full squeeze
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze**
- Torso anchored to the seat, no lifting forward; no bouncing out of the bottom

This comes BEFORE incline RDL on purpose — running it after smoked it last week. Take the leg curl fresh.

**LOAD:** 45lb plate. 3 sets of 15, dead slow with a 2s pause at the bottom.
- **Pad just below the hip crease** — NOT on the upper thigh, NOT on the stomach
- **Hip hinge** — a Romanian deadlift on the 45° bench, NOT a lumbar extension. Lower back NEUTRAL throughout
- **At the bottom:** the stretch is in the **hamstrings and glutes**, NOT the lower back. If the lumbar rounds, you're going too deep for current mobility
- **Drive up by squeezing the glutes and hamstrings**
- **At the top:** stop at neutral. Past neutral = lumbar load = QL irritation
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom, 1s drive up.** The slow eccentric is the entire reason this lift works
- Take extra rest between sets if you need it

**Reflection:** where's the stretch landing — hamstrings/glutes (correct) or lower back (too deep / pad placement off)? If lower back, slow down further and check the pad before set 2.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Recovery Block (Hip/QL-Biased for Legs Day)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Scissor the legs, reach overhead, lean away from the back leg — bookend the session with the same QL/psoas release as the warmup.
45s each side. Deep hip-flexor and glute release — the long hold lets the QL and psoas let go.
30s each side. Gentle twist for the QL — draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5-min recovery block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.

tips: **Steady state, station-grouped.** Squat 4 sets, leg press 4, calf raise 3, Bulgarian 3, leg curl 3, incline RDL 3.
**Squat holds 6/7/8/8 at 75** — depth builds across the ramp; keep working it, don't add load.
**Spotlight: leg press + Bulgarian.** Leg press drills the full-ROM core/QL depth; Bulgarian steps the load up.
**Station-grouped:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (same machine — stay there) → Bulgarian → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — don't reverse them; running incline RDL first stacked the hamstring work and smoked the leg curl.
**Bulgarian steps up** — single 45-50lb DB or a 25lb pair. Drop to bodyweight if anything twitches.
**Incline RDL is a 45lb plate, dead slow** — the tempo is the progression, not the number.
**Cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down** — QL/psoas release.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.**
Rest: 3 min squats, 2 min leg press, 90s calf raise + Bulgarian + isolations.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state legs week. The squat pattern is settled (75 / 6/7/8/8, depth builds across the ramp), so the spotlight moves to the two lifts with something to drill: leg press, where full depth has quietly become core/QL work, and the Bulgarian, where a clean step-up is earned. The sequence keeps the two hamstring lifts from stacking. Form leads load on every lift — building decades, not weeks.
